description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2024: Alternatives for Resilient Communities: A Tool to Inform Optimal Tornado Retrofits is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by William Hughes, National Institute of Standards and Technology (nist.gov). Tornadoes can devastate impacted communities, razing buildings, uprooting trees, and destroying powerlines. To effectively reduce these disasters’ catastrophic impacts, improved models are needed to help decision-makers prioritize retrofit strategies under resource constraints. The Alternatives for Resilient Communities (ARC) software, first applied to riverine flooding and seismic hazards, is here extended to address tornadic hazards. Coverage: University of Maryland. DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-0esr-0z28. Keywords: alternatives for resilient communities, community resilience, tornado adaptation, Joplin tornado, retrofit optimization, tornado shelters. Published 2024-06-28. Facility named: Center for Risk-Based Community Resilience Planning. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
